title: Two copies in one room
bodyMd:
A fictional community archive digitized its photographs and saved two copies on separate drives. Staff initially described the collection as protected from loss. A volunteer asked where the drives were kept. Both were in the same cupboard, so a fire or flood affecting that cupboard could destroy both copies.

The archive arranged an additional copy at a different location and tested whether files could actually be restored. The tests revealed a few files that had never copied correctly. Keeping copies was therefore only part of the task: independence from shared hazards and evidence of successful recovery also mattered. The archive did not promise that loss had become impossible. It replaced a simple count of copies with a more specific account of which failures its arrangements could withstand.
